english: Word reached Basium that the battle for Tempus Mor was nearing an end. The eternal war was going well in this theatre, when disaster struck. An assassin from the Astur Wastes, that dismal marshland far to the south beyond the Deruptus Mountains, took both the life and the soul of his patron. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The archangel did not mind the end of a mortal life, but he mourned the loss of a soul that should have risen to join his ranks forever. Her spirit was strong, the sort that might turn the tide of the war. He thought it was a pity that such a soul had been wasted on a mere mortal woman, rather than a True Angel, and an grave injustice that it should now serve another. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The Mercurian commander knew more of these accursed Shades than any mortal, more even than they knew of themselves. They began as a people devoted to his own creator, Arawn, although the God of Death himself was always indifferent to them. Basium knew they has betrayed their lord, and did not consider their ignorance of this fact to be a excuse. "They might not be demons," thought Basium, "or even the undead, but they are indeed a corruption that must be purged from existence. "[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Stop!" commanded Gyra, as she materialized to block her twin's path. "You shall not destroy a people under my protection! Their reverence for Arawn is strong. The Compact would not stop me from sending legions of Arawn's Dullahan to protect them!. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Basium laughed. "The Compact! What do I care about that old agreement. I rejected it from the start, and am constrained by it no more than a mortal. Besides, I lead the armies of Arawn! Do you not see them? Your pitiful band is no match for mine, and we both know that our maker would never lend you more support. He cares for the prayers of the living no more than a man cares for the prayers of a bug. Would he permit you to guard the thralls of The Pretender? I am not ignorant, dear sister. My Dullahan attest that the soul of Queen Ethne, like all the victims of the Netherblade, are bound not merely to the Netherworld, but to the Kingdom of Laroth; they are being recruited into the resistance. "[PARAGRAPH]"Remember the terms of your fall, dear brother," Gyra rejoined. "You are indeed as constrained as any mortal. Mortals die, and their souls are collected. I can see to it that this happens to you. I would gladly escort your spirit to a cell in our maker's vault. Have you seen Anesidora lately? Time has not been kind to her. Without the divine spark of The One passed down through the children of Nemed, eons as my inmate will not be kind to you either. [PARAGRAPH]Yet that would be a mercy. I should serve your warrant from The Divine Court. Dadga would not risk your escape from Alius Orbis. The portals you once guarded might only let you return here as an unborn babe. You would forget most of who you were before you grow enough to lead armies again, and in the meantime would be vulnerable to the corruptions of the flesh, but too much your purpose would remain. The Court would surely rule you must be remade, stripped of all your memories and made to wander the Wildlands as a mindless beast. Perhaps you could bow before Sucellus, swear to guard the Font of Life for the theif who stole it, and beg "the God of Daisies" so ask court for clemency? I think not. [PARAGRAPH]It is Death the Sidar worship. Arawn is in no condition to help them, but I will not turn away from that responsility. [PARAGRAPH]Take your renegade armies of Life and go. Half of them would abandon you anyway if you diverted them towards this quest. They don't serve you any more than you serve Arawn, or Sucellus. They only follow you for a chance to slay demons. Are all the demons vanquished aready? Funny, it seems like I would have noticed if the Fane of the Lesser's had been closed. No, I believe it is still in business, still trapping souls that belong to my master in order to feed the great machine of hell. Tell you what: I'll handle the Sidar my own way. I'll lead Decius to attack them and confiscate Laroth's blade, but he shall not be permitted to rule or exterminate them. They are to be left in peace after that. I shall handle Laroth myself. If that task is finished before you reach the Gates of Hell, I'll join in your assault. Would you agree to that Compact?" she teased. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Basium was not amused, but he agreed to the terms and departed with his army unto the Fane of the Lessers.

The war has been a true disaster for our people, every hardship brings with it an opportunity for new growth. It will take generations for the world to recover, but eventually all good things shall come back stronger that they were before. Now that the Mercurian armies march off to fight evils elsewhere, it is our duty to help this land recover.

The damage from this conflict was greater than expected, but at least Queen Viconia had her victory. The elven nation would soon fully submit to her, and she could focus on vanquishing her "allies. " Her assassins had already executed most of the ritualists who summoned Hyborem, and she had an amazing trap planned for the next meeting of the Undercouncil. It might not actually be possible to truly kill Os-Gabella, but she would sure enjoy seeing her try to escape from a coffin of mithril and nullstone. Forces had already been dispatched to The Dead Lands to stop Os-Gabella's ally Tebryn Arbandi from completing his world ending rituals. Faeryl looked quite pleased as she walk out onto the dais to address her court. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Just as she began her speech, the crowd was shocked to see an assassin materialize behind their queen and stab her straight through her heart. They were then surprised to see the assassin vanish as quickly as he appeared. Those who knew Faeryl were not surprised to see the illusion of her corpse dissolve shortly after the assassin had left. Soon the assassin was surprised to find himself caught in the web of a giant spider, with the real Faeryl staring down at him in glee. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Not a bad try," she said, "for a human. It's not nearly as elegant as Rivanna's last few attempts on my life, but better than some from the newer members of my personal guard. The invisibility was a nice touch, but you relied too heavily on it and got sloppy. How about you tell me who sent you so I can show your people how assassination is supposed to be done? No? Oh, well, I guess I'll just have to find some other way to have fun. "

The Overcouncil has been crushed, and the lands of Tempus Mor infected with a taint that will in time spread to merge all Erebus with hell. It has become a new Fane of the Lessers, though I shall not allow lesser demon lords access to his foothold.

O Great Lord of the Balors, an imp announced, trembling in fear before Hyborem's might. "Our ally Decius has brought his own enemies to this fight. From the Bannor lands come the Order's hunter, Valin Phanuel, hunting demons and heretics. He ambushed the sect stationed by the southern pass, and vanquished it utterly. I was allowed to escape only to deliver his threats to Commander Achare, but of course I have chosen to inform you first. "[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Enraged by the news, the archangel slammed the messenger against the palace wall, breaking his wings and causing him to cough up black blood. "Send him your message then," he said, as he hurled the dazed imp through a portal to the Calabim camp.

Our spies have informed me that the Bannor have sent a great champion of the Order to aid the Elohim in their war against the Infernal. While their welfare is not a top priority, we should ready an assassin to take him out should he venture into the Umbrawood.

Excellent news my queen: we may now have another ally. The Bannor have not yet sent the army we requested to aid in the war against the Sheaim and Infernal, but they have sent their great hero Valin Phanuel as an advance guard. He has already annihilated a sect stationed near the southern pass of Tempus Mor. This may not directly effect the battle for the Umbrawood, but it may distract Hyborem long enough for us to prepare a defense for the heartland.

Terrible news my queen: a great champion has risen up in service of the Ashen Veil. A former Bannor Oathtaker has renounced all virtue and been anointed with blood and equipped with armour bearing the darkest demonic runes. We can only hope that is grudge against our ally Decius keeps him too busy fighting the Malakim to focus his intention on the Umbrawood.

Our spies report that a renegade Bannor Oathtaker by the Rosier has just been anointed as a champion of the Ashen Veil, and now rides out against our foes. Keep and eye on him, and prepare an assassin to take his life once our mutual enemies are defeated.

The Queen of Storms has come to us to share a plan that she and the Svartalfar have devised to stir discord in the Overcouncil. We are all to keep Commander Decius out of the inner circle of the Undercouncil, isolate him and encourage his relations with the druidess Talia Gosam. To hurry this along, we have decided to let Duke Sallos send his most subtle servants to the Calabim camp to inflame the desires of their flesh.

By the Sheaim's request, the Queen of Sorrows herself has been enlisted to whisper into Talia's ear and claim her soul. Soon Varn shall loose that which he loves most, and the Overcouncil shall be broken.

Our spies have confirmed that Talia now comes often to the bed of Decius, and leaves again quite satisfied. Our progress has been reported to the Deathless Queen, who shall proceed to the next step of the operation soon.

Arendel traveled to Golden Leane to attend the meeting of the Overcouncil, and chose to stay with the druidess whom Varn had married. Although Talia seemed eager to show off the oasis and claimed to love the life their even more than the forest, Queen Phaedra was not convinced. There was clearly a loneliness within the woman's heart. Arendel believed this was from staying separated from the Fellowship for too long.

Just this front of the war on evil began to turn in our favor, the Overcouncil called a mandatory meeting to discuss the progress. Why must I waste my time listening to mortal men and women prattle on, exchanging worthless pleasantries and coy glances while there is a war to wage? I swear that these mortals have too much of the spirit of compromise in them. I made it clear that I would not let them be such fools as to end this war early, and then stormed out.
Ethne began to explain to the Mercurian commander why the Speaker of the Overcouncil had recently been changed, but he dismissed the matter as trivial mortal politics and returned to the front lines.
Arendel was surprised to at the absence of both Varn and Talia Gosam from the latest Overcouncil meeting, but was too polite to ask why the other elves were missing.
Haste - the first level Body spell increases the movement rate of living units.

Pit Beast - The demon summoned by the second level Chaos spell is reasonably strong, and may start with all sorts of useful (or not no useful) random promotions, and their duration is extended with each living unit they kill. Beware though, because Pit Beasts are notoriously disloyal and hard to control. They may fight for you one turn, and against you the next.

You suddenly feel like a much younger man. No longer so set in your ways, you mind has been opened to learn from the unexpected. Surely this is the blessing of Amathaon. [PARAGRAPH]All spheres of magic have Affinity promotions that allow different spells with different Channeling promotions, but Creation is the only sphere where spells can only be cast with affinity. There is no Creation I, Creation II, or Creation III promotion that arcane units with access to Creation mana can learn from experience. The Creation spells are Muse, Summon Pixie, and Abundance. Muse and Abundance are very useful in cities but useless in dungeons. Pixies act like workers who can be sacrificed for production, culture, or research, but their only real value in this scenario is their ability to create Illusions to act as decoys. [PARAGRAPH]The main value of Creation affinity in this scenario is that the promotion may randomly grant you a Potion of Restoration, which can be used to heal your unit, remove any negative promotions, and restore casting ability.

Escape - The first level dimensional spell allows you to teleport yourself directly home to your capital city, or, in the case of this scenario, out of the Cave of the Ancestors. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Your trial is complete!
Stoneskin - The second level Earth sphere spell allows you to build up a thick defensive layer of earth to wear as a second skin. This significantly improves your ability to withstand enemy attacks.
Enchanted Blade - The first level Enchantment spell allows you to enhance the weapons of melee units. It will not help Dain directly, but may improve some of his summons.

Rust - The first Entropy spell allows you to quickly corrode your enemy's weapons. It removed the Bronze Weapons, Iron Weapons, and Mithril Weapons promotions, and adds the Rusted promotion which makes enemies 10% weaker. Note however that Rusted is only applied to Melee units.
Temperance - the basic Force spell allows you to maintain such a balance as to be able to resist damage both holy and unholy
Slow - The basic Ice sphere spell gives enemy units a promotion that reduces their movement by one point. It can take some time to wear off, granting you or denying them a chance to run away.
Summon Einherjar - The mid tier Law spell allows you to summon an angel who can guard your caster and gains increased duration whenever it defeats an enemy.
Destroy Undead - The mid level Death spell directly deals Holy damage to units of the Undead race. Note that it does not discriminate friend from foe, and can harm your own undead summons as well.
Charm - The mid level Mind spell renders enemy units unable to attack, leaving them to wander around harmlessly.

Bloom - The Nature 2 spell allows you to create a New Forest feature on the caster's tile. This will eventually grow into a normal Forest and if you have the Fellowship of the Leaves state religion may then grow into an Ancient Forest. This probably is not the most useful spell within a dungeon, however.
Shadowwalk - The mid level Shadow spell allows you to use enemy roads, ignore the defenses of enemy buildings, and have a chance to withdraw from combat when you would otherwise be defeated.
Blinding Light - The second Sun spell allows you to temporarily blind your opponents, rendering them immobile until their vision returns.
There is a meta magic rune on the door ahead. As you approach the rune flares up and pushes you back.

The Grigori people rallied to their own defense with greater ardor that the Illians and Doviello had ever thought possible. Their combined forces were mighty, but a few brave adventurers repeatedly drove them back. It seems now that Cassiel may never be vanquished by a mere mortal. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Fortunately for Auric, the Philosopher-King was not the only archangel left in Erebus either. There are two who have been confined here for ages, betrayed by their own creators and forever denied an ara of protection. Though it takes great might to break through the prisons of the gods, the captives within would make a worthy sacrifice. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Arise Odio! The malice of modern man is great. As I channel it to you now it breathes breathes life back into your stony flesh. The Curse of Kilmorph shall not hold you long! Aeron abandoned you to her, but you have a new master now. Behold thy new god!"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The heart of Odio ignited and the muscles of his chest began to ripple, but he was still mostly rock, unable to see much less free himself. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The earth trembled as he uttered the words "How may I serve you my lord?"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]With a sinister grin, Auric replied; "With your immortal soul. "[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]He plunged a copper dagger deep within the helpless demon's heart, and reveled as a stream of the foulest blood washed over him. Odio's screams caused distant mountains to collapse, but Auric was unmoved. Slowly, carefully, he completed the spell by pushing the daggers blade into his right hand, cutting his flesh and allowing his blood to mix with the dead archangel. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]In that moment, in a thousand different places in Erebus prophets received visions of a Winter Wyrm swallowing the world. Priests were overcome with a sense of foreboding and a cool wind blew through even the warmest areas. Auric's ascension had begun.

Thy starlight bonds are soon to be dissolved. The dark passion of your fallen mistress shall not go unopposed. Your service here will be invaluable. "[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"How may I serve your righteous cause," she intoned, with a melody that could fill all but the coldest hearts with love. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Righteous? Who said the cause was Righteous?" Auric grinned. " I am here to restore the ancient order, to return Winter to ascendancy. The flames of passion will have no place there, but are of use to be now. You shall serve me with your dying breath!"[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Auric hurled the copper dagger from his side directly at the archangel's heart. It struck true. Brigit cried out less in pain than in exertion as he directed all her power at him in the form of white hot flames. Auric merely stepped back and allowed the Ring of Carcer to absorb the entire force of the blow. By the time the barrier had fully collapsed, Brigit lay helpless on the ground, completely exhausted. Auric strode forth and leaned over her dying form. He twisted the blade and watched the last of her shimmering blood drain out. Slowly, carefully, he completed the spell by pushing the daggers blade into his right hand, cutting his flesh and allowing his blood to mix with the dead archangel. Priests were overcome with a sense of foreboding and a cool wind blew through even the warmest areas. Auric's ascension had begun.

Our scouts have found the location of the legendary Ring of Carcer! It is said that this is the prison where Bhall trapped her archangel Brigit the Shining when she refused to fall with her mistress. If we can get a unit strong enough to enter the Ring and free her, then we can use her blood for Auric's ritual.

Our scouts have found the location of Odio's Prison! It is said that this great stone statue is actually the petrified form of Aeron's archangel. Odio was trapped like this as punishment for defying his lord's orders and going on a rampage against the worshipers of Kilmorph during the time of the truce that led to the signing of The Compact. If we can get a unit strong enough to free him, then his blood would be enough for Auric to complete his ritual.

Description: Tebryn means to destroy the world. He has gathered his generals around him and has bent the power of the Dead Lands to his control. If Armageddon is to be prevented Tebryn must be stopped here. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Special Rules: Human units won't heal in this scenario. Human units that die are reborn as undead units under Tebryn's control. Tebryn's lands can't be entered until all the other Sheaim players are defeated. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Requires: Successful completion of the Radiant Guard scenario.

Malakim, Age of Rebirth, Chaos 3[PARAGRAPH]High priest of the Sons of Discord. One of the seven Aspects of War.[PARAGRAPH]A Calabim attack wiped out Seth's Malakim village when he was a boy. Alone, he retaliated, striking night after night at Calabim camps, forts and villages. Killing indiscriminately. He killed hundreds, and those that chased him out into the desert never returned. Among the Calabim he became known as "Dreamstealer" because he killed so many in their sleep. Most believed him to be a ghost or demon, not a teenage boy.[PARAGRAPH]Eventually Seth was caught (though they didn't know he was Dreamstealer) and placed in a Calabim slave mine. He toiled in that mine for 3 long years, making friends with only one other slave, a man named Petr. It was then that Camulos called to him, to form a new church upon Erebus. Seth accepted that call and cut out Petr's heart and sacrificed it to Camulos. In response Camulos caused a rage to fall upon the slaves and they rose up against the slavemasters. During that fight Seth escaped from the mine.[PARAGRAPH]Tired of the Calabim and the desert he traveled acting as a mercenary and assassin, and spent time among the Hippus and Lanun. He gathered men as he went and made them disciples of Camulos, forcing them to fight each other to the death to join his church. Forging his church from the bloody arena floor.

*Revolutions Mod Hint*: The Revolution Watch Advisor screen is totally customisable in the same way as the Domestic Advisor Screen.
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: Customise the Revolution Watch Advisor to suit your playing style and imagination! Put the culture level column next to the Revolution trend column, it doesn't matter!

*Revolutions Mod Hint*: The Revolution Watch Advisor can also display important buildings constructed in a city that are relevant to Revolutions, especially cultural buildings like wonders, and theatres!
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: City bribing can be initiated from the city screen or the Revolutions Watch Advisor screen.
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: The civ info screen can now graph the overall revolt stability of your empire, or your enemies empire! You just need sufficient espionage points...
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: Pay attention to the underlying rebellion issues in your city! If the citizens are sick of slavery, you may need to do something about it or accept the consequences!
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: Play Revolutions with an experimental mindset. Cause and effect are not necessarily immediately obvious...
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: If you decide to go to war, make sure you have the peoples support! If you have chosen a bad target or get bogged down in the war, the people may drop their support for you!
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: Running a deficit economy for too long, can make the people's approval of you decline. If you destroy the economy, you could well be destroyed!
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: Spend a surplus wisely. If you waste it, you may not have the money to buy bribes or pay for civic infrastructure vital to keep the people placid.
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: Think of yourself at all times as being a servant of your people. They are your boss, whether you are running a democracy or a dictatorship!
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: In Revolutions, your potential opponent is not just your rival civ, but your own people...
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: If your overall empire domestic stability is good, the world is your oyster!
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: When you have domestic problems, think of what has happened in real history to deal with those problems. It is no different in the game!
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: At some point, underlying rebellion can explode into violence no matter what you do. Be ready with law enforcement troops if needed!
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: If you face a revolt, don't panic. So long as you are not in the middle of a foreign war, you can apply military force on the rebels and gain experience!

*Revolutions Mod Hint*: To protect your unstable cities, make sure you have law enforcement entrenched, and law enforcement units around the city too! Rebels will burn the countryside not just the city!
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: If a rebellion emerges, remember that not all rebels are visible. Rebel spies can do damage if you are not prepared...

*Revolutions Mod Hint*: If you are overthrown and the citizens demand a new leader, it is not all bad. You will loose control of your empire for a time, but after this time you will have a new and interesting scenario to deal with.
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: Bribing dissidents and city officials can buy you important time to deal with regional discontent!
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: If you decide that you need to deal with rebellion with bribery, remember that your corruption does not go unwatched...
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: Bribery is an important strategic element in advanced Revolutions play.
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: If you pay out cash to one city in order to keep it quiet, other cities may increase their disloyalty too...unless you pay up to them as well!
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: Beware of the Domino Effect...If one city rebels, this can cascade into a regional or empire wide rebellion!
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: If a rebel movement has taken control of parts of your empire, do not be frustrated! Patiently wait until the time is right and hit back at the rebellion with your loyal army!
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: If parts of your empire have broken away under independent rule, make sure their leaders do not side with your enemies!
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: The speed of city growth is an important element in controlling the stability of your empire. Grow too big too fast and their will be rogue elements emerging, be sure of that!
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: The speed of city growth is one important aspect of advanced Revolutions game play. Keep city growth capped if need be, but not too long either!
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: The loyalty of the citizenry is more easily kept in check in a tightly knit well connected empire.
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: Without question, the most difficult aspect of Revolutions management, is the issue of distant settlements and colonies. These need special attention.
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: It is a common misconception that you cannot expand into a mighty global empire under Revolutions. You can! You just have to do it right!
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: War gathers it's own momentum, not just in conquest, but in the approval of your citizens. Keep it rolling with rewards for them, and they will support you!
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: Religion plays a huge role in the stability of your society. Try to run your civics to match the religious needs of your society.

*Revolutions Mod Hint*: If you are faced with an empire with many different faiths, fear not! So long as you don't attempt to run a theocracy or organised religious state, the people may really respect you!
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: If you want religious purity in your empire, do it wisely but be extra vigilant to non-state religions taking hold!
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: Without question, the management of holy city sites is one of the biggest challenges in Revolutions.
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: Under Revolutions you can hold firm more than one holy city in your empire. Two holy cities is fine, the challenge accumulates as the number of holy sites increase!
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: The tools you have to manage Revolutions are many. Civics, culture, surplus cash, infrastructure, wonders, military, luxuries, war success are but a few.

*Revolutions Mod Hint*: It is a common misconception that Revolutions fundamentally changes the basic game play. It does not. It merely adds another strategic layer upon the game, the management of your people...
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: Keep in mind the distinction between the general apathetic citizenry who are dictated by happiness and health, from the dissident minorities that have their own agendas.
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: A city may appear to be happy, but this may only be a surface manifestation. If their are many foreign nationals, the desire for independence by force can emerge anyway!
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: Distant settlements need special attention. Give them extras like cultural assets, defence assets and military support to ensure that you are looking after them!
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: Your citizens like constant improvements to their circumstances. Stagnation is your biggest enemy, not the people!
*Revolutions Mod Hint*:In big empires, it is often better to let a city or even a region break away. The break always may be weak and exploitable.

*Revolutions Mod Hint*: In Revolutions, you may think that it is the end for a leader and a nation if they are defeated. But it may not be! Leaders will go underground and re-emerge rather than be destroyed for all time.
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: If you want to conquest an enemy, make sure you get every last one of them! Even a single remainder can re-emerge as a resistance movement!
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: A cultural victory strategy has a spin off in Revolutions. The people will love you and you may wait for rival super powers to implode...

*Revolutions Mod Hint*: If word spreads that an empire has collapsed into anarchy and rebellion, try to exploit it. These foreign citizens can be won over to your cause more easily than if you were to conquest that empire.

*Revolutions Mod Hint*: Without question, capturing cities and holding them is more difficult in Revolutions. Military strategy must always keep in mind long term domestic stability of newly acquired territories.
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: A long term unstable settlement along way from home is not a bad thing. So long as there is strong military presence, medium term cycles of anarchy are manageable.
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: Distant holy city sites are always going to be tricky to hold unless you concede at least in part, to the faith of that city.
*Barbarian Civ Hint*: It is not always wise to eliminate every last barbarian city before they evolve into minor civs. You may need trading partners!
*Barbarian Civ Hint*: Start a game with only yourself! Competitors will emerge. Just make sure you turn off conquest and domination victory conditions!

*Barbarian Civ Hint*: If a barbarian city emerges as a minor civilization, don't despair. Farm them accordingly and pounce on them if they are weak, for more rewards than if they had remained as barbarians!
*Barbarian Civ Hint*: Barbarians evolve into minor civilizations. Minor civilizations evolve into full blooded civilizations. At each stage, they get stronger, economically and militarily.

*Barbarian Civ Hint*: If you are all alone on a continent, encourage not just one minor nation to emerge, but at least a third. You may need to trade in a tri-pact relationship. Binary pacts rarely work.
*Barbarian Civ Hint*: If a minor civ emerges in your region, be warned that your outlying settlements may begin to become more loyal to them, not you!
*Barbarian Civ Hint*: The emergence of minor civs with capable armies may appear unfair, but remember that they need something to ensure a chance of long term survival.
*Barbarian Civ Hint*: A minor civ does all the things a full civ does, but is more primitive in sophistication. A minor civ is insular and will not talk with you for example.
*Barbarian Civ Hint*: Yes it is irritating if a minor civ settles vast fields of wild dye, leaving you without!
*Barbarian Civ Hint*: New world maps are great. The old world you are on will one day discover a fully viable new world that has evolved of itself.
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: Try the game options "Start as Minors". If you like early warfare, it is the option of choice!
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: There is no conspiracy in the "Start as Minors" option. You will make friends if you are influential enough!
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: Lacking a little spice in your life? Try "Start as Minors" with "Aggressive AI". That should do it!

*Revolutions Mod Hint*: Revolutions games are more interesting and diverse than standard games. It is well worth writing down your game history turn by turn, in the autolog with the [ALT E] keystroke.

*Revolutions Mod Hint*: Hereditary Rule is not necessarily the answer to all your revolt problems! The character of this political system will mean that war will have to be more carefully thought out to win your kingdom's support.
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: Despotism is a viable option! A despot has less ethical issues to deal with so long as his people can be kept in the dark about them! A despot can win wars when a King cannot!
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: Pay particular attention to the labour reforms your society adopts. It is these that the people must work under!
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: The Sevopedia now displays revolutions specific civic effects and leader traits can be customised for revolution effects!
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: Don't be scared to run slavery! The citizens will endure the whipping.....for a time!
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: Really, in a diverse religious state, you wouldn't run organised religion, would you?
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: If you really want democracy, have it! But reform doesn't end there!
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: Switching to a police state may be good at times of instability! How else can you keep the empire under your thumb?
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: There is nothing more fun than to slowly destabilise a super power by stagnating it, and to grab the spoils when it implodes!
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: Che Guevara is the symbol for this mod! Play the game like he did, and you should be fine!
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: If you are sick of constant rebellious uprisings against you, don't forget [CTRL-SHIFT-L] and you can switch over to the rebels side!
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: If you think about it, a mod that makes the game more difficult like Revolutions, also makes the game more rewarding...
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: If you have stabilised your domestic society and you are the leader the people want, any standard BTS strategy is available for you to implement.
*DCM Hint*: Catapults cannot range bombard.
*DCM Hint*: Range bombarding cities has a slightly different effect to bombarding them directly. Range bombarding aims fire at the defenders of the city as well as the defences!
*DCM Hint*: Range bombarding cities has much less impact on the defenders than the defences of the city. Defenders can seek cover even behind damaged walls!....for a time...
*DCM Hint*: If you want to take down a cities defences at maximum thrift, just straight bombard the city defences and leave the defenders until there is no where for them to hide.

*DCM Hint*: If you are defending your precious city from an enemy stack, range bombard the attackers as best you can from inside the city, but remember that your accuracy is compromised by being behind city structures and impediments.
*DCM Hint*: Properly set-up defensive structures like forts or field deployments with properly constructed frontlines, are by far the most effective way to range bombard.
*DCM Hint*: Range bombard now only issues standard BTS collateral damage upon stacks. It is completely useless against single units and siege as well as the head defender of the enemy stack.

*DCM Hint*: When thinking about range bombardment and how it causes damage, imagine the battle scenario. Range bombard tends to hit the main throng of the enemy army, missing the frontline attackers and not reaching the counter siege at the rear!
*DCM Hint*: Range bombardment effect can be customised in GlobalDefinesAlt.xml

*Revolutions Mod Hint*: Try the Barbarian world option where barbs sometimes start with cities in place at game start! This can make them more competitive but also give you a nice early target for conquest!
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: Revolutions and it's components are configurable and customisable in Revolution.ini

*Revolutions Mod Hint*: If you want an interesting variation of Revolutions, that effectively turns down the overall difficulty of the mod, try the "Inquisitions" option or "Limited Religions" or both!
*Revolutions Mod Hint*: From most difficult to least difficult are: Straight Revolutions, Limited Religions or Inquisitions, Limited Religion and Inquisitions.
*Influence Driven War*: If you need to ensure you keep your borders intact, you may have to get out from behind city fortification and fight in the field!

*Influence Driven War*: If you have a choice of where you want to fight, pick a location that will be most useful to you so that if you win the battle, your influence around the battle region is good enough to keep the territory!
*Influence Driven War*: Keep an eye out for the culture mix of the tile you are contesting. It is possible that a 5% influence swing to you may be enough to win the territory!

*RevolutionDCM*: If you select the "debug" option under the RevDCM tab, game options will update on the next turn!
*RevolutionDCM*: Some game options like enabling or disabling Revolutions, can only be done at the start of a game in the custom game screen.

Introduction to the Revolution Mod

Welcome to the Revolution![NEWLINE][NEWLINE]This mod consists of several different pieces which work together to make Civ4 more dynamic, with empires rising and falling more throughout the game.  Below are some brief descriptions and hints for playing with this mod:[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]
Revolution

This is the main component of the mod and affects the internal stability of your and every other empire.  Keeping the citizens of your empire content is now a bigger issue, as if a city feels they have been mistreated they may rebel against you!  The new Revolution Watch screen can help you keep track of how your citizens are feeling and can be opened either by using the button below the advisor buttons or by pressing Ctrl+Shift+W.  This screen shows which cities are feeling rebelious and why they do or don't like your current policies.  This info can also be found in the city screen near the culture bar and moving your cursor over the new Revolut Status bar will bring up specific information about the city.  There are many different reasons why your citizens can love or hate living in your empire and keeping them happy and patriotic adds a new dimension to managing your empire.  One tool you have if you need to buy time or avoid a pending revolt is the ability to make a large cash 'donation' to a city, the options for this can be accessed either through the Revolution Watch screen or by clicking on the Revolt Status bar in the city screen.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]If some of your citizens disagree with your policies or want to separate from your empire, you'll be presented with a popup offering you a choice on how to respond to their demands.  There are many different kinds of demands your citizens may make, from changes to your civics to complete freedom on cultural or religious grounds, and for each type of revolt there are multiple ways you can respond.  You can always avoid outright war or force the separatists to fight for their freedom.  If you defeat them on the battle field, they will think twice before revolting again.  However, you will eventually need to address the issues that cause them to revolt or potentially face a protracted civil war.  Your allies and enemies will also face the possibilities of open revolts, which can present opportunities for you in many different ways and other leaders can also lose elections or be forced to cede power control of their empire to another leader.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Playing with Revolution may require you to adjust your strategies for building up your empire or conquering foreign territory.  Some general guidelines are that building your culture and spreading your religion are now more important to help keep your empire cohesive.  Strong defenses and victory in war can also keep your empire doing well.  Over expansion is more risky and an empire that spends too much commerce on taxes will not last for long.  Picking civics that suit your empire is also important.  Check the Revolution Watch screen and the status bars in your cities to see what issues your citizens have and head them off before they boil over into open revolt.
